results.name: Barri Gòtic (Gothic Quarter)
results.character: Medieval labyrinth of narrow alleys, Gothic churches, and hidden squares right in the city centre
results.what_to_do_there: Visit Barcelona Cathedral, explore the Roman ruins beneath Plaça del Rei (MUHBA), wander through the ancient Jewish quarter (El Call), and people-watch at palm-lined Plaça Reial
results.why_it_is_special: Built on the remains of the Roman colony of Barcino, it is the oldest part of the city — every alley tells a story spanning over 2,000 years

results.name: El Born / La Ribera
results.character: Trendy yet medieval; Renaissance palaces sit alongside designer boutiques, gourmet shops, and art galleries
results.what_to_do_there: See the Basílica de Santa Maria del Mar (masterpiece of Catalan Gothic), stroll Carrer Montcada's 14th–18th-century palaces, visit the Picasso Museum, and browse independent fashion showrooms
results.why_it_is_special: Once the merchants' quarter during Barcelona's 13th–14th-century maritime expansion, it is now considered the city's "Montmartre" for its creative scene

results.name: Gràcia
results.character: Bohemian, village-like feel with lively squares, eco-shops, yoga studios, and vegan-friendly cafés
results.what_to_do_there: Visit Park Güell and Casa Vicens (Gaudí's first house), stroll Carrer Verdi for indie cinemas and bars, browse edgy galleries, and relax in Plaça de la Virreina
results.why_it_is_special: A former independent town absorbed into Barcelona in the 19th century, it retains its own distinctly Catalan identity and a relaxed, creative atmosphere

results.name: Barceloneta
results.character: Classic seaside fishing quarter with narrow streets, laundry lines between buildings, and a lively beachfront promenade
results.what_to_do_there: Walk the Mediterranean promenade, eat fresh seafood tapas at traditional restaurants, visit Mercat de la Barceloneta, and swim at the city's oldest beach
results.why_it_is_special: A former fishermen's village transformed for the 1992 Olympics; it is said to have inspired Cervantes as the setting for Don Quixote's fight with the Knight of the White Moon

results.name: El Poble-Sec
results.character: Working-class, close-knit community at the foot of Montjuïc; a blend of tradition and bohemia that rarely sees tourists
results.what_to_do_there: Sample legendary tapas at Quimet & Quimet, explore the Civil War air-raid shelter Refugi 307, ride the Montjuïc cable car, and enjoy summer performances at the open-air Teatre Grec
results.why_it_is_special: Barcelona's first expansion beyond the medieval walls; nicknamed "Little Paris" in the 1940s for its cabarets, and birthplace of singer-songwriter Joan Manuel Serrat
